summary: Module 5 DECIDE. Decision 1 (triage_priority = B, recorded via CLI): communicate first, fix second. For a SEV1 data breach, B is mandatory -- silence during a data breach compounds damage: the VP escalates in panic, customers lose trust, the security team cannot start coordination, and a wrong first fix (common under pressure) leaves no trail. The 60-second structured update (acknowledge, SEV level, knowns, unknowns, next action, ETA) costs minutes, not 15, because it is written from muscle memory; 'do both' concretely means a 60-second status update FIRST, then hands on keyboard. Decision 2 (communication_cadence = B/15-min with floor-plus-trigger): a scheduled heartbeat every 10-15 minutes guarantees stakeholders never wait in silence, and any state change (root cause, fix, rollback, resolved) fires an immediate update regardless of schedule. Rejected 5-minute cadence because the module's own math shows it burns 12+ of every 30 minutes writing updates; rejected state-change-only because 20 minutes of silence reads as 'nobody is working'. The schedule is a floor, not the whole story.
